To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method that is able to identify the skeleton of a Gaussian DAG from data under the assumption of ordered and partially ordered variables; our method compares favorably to current state of art frequentist approaches for ordered variables; it is able to deal effectively with small data sets and to learn the skeleton of the graph also under moderate mis specification of the ordering of the observed variables.

we have developed an objective Bayesian method to estimate the DAG skeleton of Gaussian models with ordered variables and non local priors, which compares favorably to the PC algorithm and to other frequentist methods, and is robust to moderate mis specifications of the ordering of the nodes.

we propose a novel objective Bayesian search of Gaussian DAG models for ordered variables, based on a non local prior for the precision matrices, and we demonstrate that it compares favorably with the PC algorithm in terms of the edge hit rate versus the false alarm rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of Gaussian directed acyclcic graphical models from data and with the assessment of the robustness of the method to misspecification of the ordering of the observed variables.

developing an objective Bayesian approach for learning Gaussian DAG models for ordered variables, which provides a flexible, efficient, and competitive alternative to current state of practice methods.
the problem of identifying the skeleton of a Gaussian DAG, under a given ordering of the variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is a powerful and versatile tool to learn the structure of Gaussian DAG models with ordered variables.
the proposed method is competitive with state of the art methods for the estimation of the skeleton of the graph, and is superior to them when the variables are assumed ordered.

the objective Bayesian approach proposed here, with the appropriate non local priors, is a promising alternative to the PC algorithm for learning the skeleton, and a competitive alternative to frequentist methods for learning the DAG, when a known ordering of variables is available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for learning sparse DAGs that performs well in a variety of settings, and is especially suited for data sets with a small number of variables and observations.
we propose a novel Bayesian method for learning Gaussian DAG models, based on a non local parameter prior, which is especially well suited for learning sparse networks.
the method proposed here provides a flexible and effective tool to learn the skeleton of a DAG, which could be useful for the analysis of data from physical and biological systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the variables are known to be ordered, objective Bayesian methods are competitive with the current state of the frequentist art, even if the order is only moderately mis-specified.
, in the context of Gaussian DAG models for ordered variables, objective Bayesian methods can be competitive with frequentist ones.

objective Bayesian search can provide a useful alternative to frequentist approaches in the context of learning Gaussian DAG models, especially when the number of variables is large and the sample size is small.
